domains.name: Standard English Conventions
domains.blurb: Editing sentences so they follow the core rules of sentence structure, usage, and punctuation.

skills.name: Sentence boundaries
skills.desc: Fragments, run-ons, and comma splices; joining or separating independent clauses correctly.

skills.name: Semicolons, colons, and commas between clauses
skills.desc: Choosing among a period, semicolon, colon, comma-plus-conjunction, or no punctuation between clauses and parts of sentences.

skills.name: Nonessential elements and supplements
skills.desc: Setting off nonessential phrases and clauses with matched commas, dashes, or parentheses; leaving essential elements unpunctuated.

skills.name: Items in a series
skills.desc: Commas and semicolons in lists; colons that introduce lists; no stray punctuation between subject and verb or verb and object.

skills.name: Subject-verb agreement
skills.desc: Matching verb to subject across intervening phrases, inverted order, compound and collective subjects, and indefinite pronouns.

skills.name: Pronoun agreement and clarity
skills.desc: Pronouns that agree with their antecedents in number and person, with a clear antecedent.

skills.name: Pronoun case
skills.desc: Subject vs. object forms (I/me, who/whom), including in compounds and comparisons.

skills.name: Verb tense, aspect, and form
skills.desc: Consistent and logical tense; finite verbs vs. participles; irregular forms; conditional and subjunctive.

skills.name: Modifier placement
skills.desc: Dangling and misplaced modifiers; the subject that follows an introductory modifying phrase.

skills.name: Parallel structure
skills.desc: Matching grammatical forms in lists, pairs, and comparisons.

skills.name: Possessives, plurals, and apostrophes
skills.desc: Plural vs. possessive nouns; its/it's, their/there/they're, whose/who's.

skills.name: Logical comparison
skills.desc: Comparing like with like ('than that of'); comparative vs. superlative forms.

skills.name: Commonly confused words
skills.desc: Affect/effect, than/then, fewer/less, among/between, and other usage pairs.

domains.name: Expression of Ideas
domains.blurb: Revising text so it says what the writer means, in the right order, at the right length, for a stated purpose.

skills.name: Transitions
skills.desc: Choosing the transition word or phrase that reflects the logical relationship between ideas.

skills.name: Rhetorical synthesis
skills.desc: Given a set of notes, choose the sentence that best accomplishes a stated rhetorical goal.

skills.name: Conciseness and redundancy
skills.desc: Eliminating wordiness and repeated ideas without losing meaning.

skills.name: Precise word choice
skills.desc: Selecting the word that fits the meaning, register, and tone of the passage.

skills.name: Style and tone consistency
skills.desc: Keeping voice, formality, and tone consistent with the rest of the passage.

skills.name: Adding, deleting, and relevance
skills.desc: Whether a sentence should be added or deleted, and why, given the paragraph's purpose.

skills.name: Organization and placement
skills.desc: Logical order of sentences and paragraphs; where a sentence best belongs.

skills.name: Introductions, conclusions, and purpose
skills.desc: Choosing sentences that open, close, or achieve a specific purpose in a paragraph or essay.

domains.name: Craft and Structure
domains.blurb: Understanding words in context and how texts are built and why.

skills.name: Words in context
skills.desc: The meaning of a high-utility word or phrase as used in a passage; the word that best completes a text.

skills.name: Text structure and purpose
skills.desc: The overall structure of a text and the function of a sentence or part within it.

skills.name: Cross-text connections
skills.desc: How two texts on the same topic relate: agreement, disagreement, response.

skills.name: Point of view and tone
skills.desc: The author's or narrator's perspective, attitude, and purpose.

domains.name: Information and Ideas
domains.blurb: Finding, interpreting, and using what a text and its graphics actually say.

skills.name: Central ideas and details
skills.desc: The main idea of a text and the details that support it.

skills.name: Command of evidence: textual
skills.desc: Which piece of text best supports, illustrates, or weakens a claim.

skills.name: Command of evidence: quantitative
skills.desc: Using data from a table or graph to complete or evaluate a claim.

skills.name: Inferences
skills.desc: The conclusion that most logically follows from a text.

skills.name: Sequence, comparison, and cause-effect
skills.desc: Relationships between events, ideas, and characters in a passage.

skills.name: Arguments and claims
skills.desc: Identifying claims, reasoning, and how evidence is used across a text or texts.

domains.name: Algebra
domains.blurb: Linear equations, functions, systems, and inequalities.

skills.name: Linear equations in one variable
skills.desc: Solving and interpreting linear equations in one variable.

skills.name: Linear functions
skills.desc: Slope, intercepts, rate of change, and linear models in tables, graphs, and equations.

skills.name: Linear equations in two variables
skills.desc: Graphs and equations of lines; parallel and perpendicular lines; interpreting coefficients.

skills.name: Systems of two linear equations
skills.desc: Solving systems; number of solutions; setting up systems from word problems.

skills.name: Linear inequalities
skills.desc: Inequalities in one or two variables, their graphs, and constraints in context.

domains.name: Advanced Math
domains.blurb: Nonlinear equations, expressions, and functions — quadratic, exponential, polynomial, rational, radical.

skills.name: Equivalent expressions
skills.desc: Rewriting, factoring, expanding, and simplifying algebraic expressions including exponents and radicals.

skills.name: Nonlinear equations and systems
skills.desc: Solving quadratic, rational, radical, and exponential equations; systems mixing linear and nonlinear equations.

skills.name: Quadratic functions
skills.desc: Vertex, roots, factored and standard forms, discriminant, and graphs of parabolas.

skills.name: Exponential functions
skills.desc: Growth and decay, interpreting parameters, and comparing linear to exponential change.

skills.name: Polynomial, rational, and radical functions
skills.desc: Zeros and end behavior of polynomials; domains and asymptotes of rational functions; radical functions.

skills.name: Function notation and transformations
skills.desc: Evaluating and composing functions; shifts, stretches, and reflections of graphs.

domains.name: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis
domains.blurb: Ratios, percentages, statistics, probability, and reasoning from data.

skills.name: Ratios, rates, proportions, and units
skills.desc: Proportional reasoning, unit conversion, and rates in context.

skills.name: Percentages
skills.desc: Percent of, percent change, and repeated percent change.

skills.name: One-variable data
skills.desc: Mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation, and distribution shape from tables and dot plots.

skills.name: Two-variable data and scatterplots
skills.desc: Lines of best fit, correlation, and interpreting models.

skills.name: Probability
skills.desc: Simple, compound, and conditional probability, often from two-way tables.

skills.name: Inference and margin of error
skills.desc: Sample statistics, population estimates, and what a margin of error means.

skills.name: Evaluating statistical claims
skills.desc: Random sampling, random assignment, and the conclusions each does and does not justify.

domains.name: Geometry and Trigonometry
domains.blurb: Shapes, angles, triangles, circles, and right-triangle trigonometry.

skills.name: Area and volume
skills.desc: Area, perimeter, surface area, and volume of common figures and solids.

skills.name: Lines, angles, and triangles
skills.desc: Angle relationships, triangle properties, similarity, and congruence.

skills.name: Right triangles and trigonometry
skills.desc: Pythagorean theorem, special right triangles, and sine, cosine, tangent.

skills.name: Circles
skills.desc: Arcs, sectors, chords, tangents, and equations of circles.

skills.name: Coordinate geometry
skills.desc: Distance, midpoint, and figures on the coordinate plane.

domains.name: Additional ACT Math
domains.blurb: Topics the ACT tests that the SAT does not.

skills.name: Number and quantity
skills.desc: Number properties, complex numbers, matrices, and vectors.

skills.name: Logarithms
skills.desc: Log properties and solving exponential equations with logs.

skills.name: Sequences and series
skills.desc: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and sums.

skills.name: Trigonometric functions
skills.desc: Unit circle, radians, graphs and identities beyond right triangles.

skills.name: Conics and advanced graphs
skills.desc: Ellipses, hyperbolas, and less common function graphs.

domains.name: Scientific Reasoning
domains.blurb: Reading data, understanding experiments, and weighing scientific arguments. Optional on the ACT; also sharpens the SAT's quantitative-evidence questions.

act.also: Scientific Investigation; Evaluating Scientific Arguments and Models with Evidence

sat.note: overlaps with command of quantitative evidence

skills.name: Interpreting data
skills.desc: Reading values, trends, and relationships from graphs and tables; interpolation and extrapolation.

skills.name: Experimental design
skills.desc: Variables, controls, procedures, and what changing a design would do.

skills.name: Evaluating arguments and models
skills.desc: Whether data support or weaken a hypothesis; comparing conflicting viewpoints.

domains.name: Essay
domains.blurb: The optional ACT Writing test: an argumentative essay responding to multiple perspectives.

skills.name: Ideas and analysis
skills.desc: A clear thesis that engages the given perspectives.

skills.name: Development and support
skills.desc: Reasoning and examples that develop the argument.

skills.name: Organization
skills.desc: Logical structure with clear transitions.

skills.name: Language use and conventions
skills.desc: Precise, varied language with sound grammar.
